_meta.confidence: High -- transcribed directly from the district's own published, adopted budget tables (GF Revenue/Expense Summary, General Fund Revenue detail, General Fund by Function). All three tables reconcile exactly to the same $21,680,639 General Fund total.

budget_message_highlights: Direct quote: 'School districts in Oregon are funded based on student enrollment. BHSD continues to experience a slow, long-term decline in enrollment. Fewer students result in less funding, which requires careful planning and ongoing adjustments to staffing levels.' -- an explicit, district-stated confirmation of the enrollment-based funding mechanism explained elsewhere in this project.

The 2025-2026 budget cuts 11 licensed positions (teaching and administrative) and 4.75 classified/managerial positions, through a combination of attrition and reduction in force, directly tied to declining enrollment.

The district expects to need an additional $1.7 million in further reductions in the second half of the 2025-27 biennium, since two things propping up this year's budget -- a $750,000 one-time payment of previously delayed forest fee revenue (2017-2021) and a $2.8 million fund carryover -- are one-time, not recurring.
The district is deliberately tapering its reserve fund from about 12% of expenditures (end of 2024-25) toward a Board target of 7.5%, planning to end 2025-26 around 8%.

For 2025-26, BHSD has access to 49% of its 2025-27 biennial State School Fund allocation (the statewide SSF is proposed at $11.36 billion for the biennium) -- consistent with the 49/51 biennial split Central Curry's budget message also referenced.

intermediate.note: 'Intermediate sources' is this district's own category label -- revenue that passes through an intermediate government unit (the county or the Education Service District) rather than coming directly from the state or a local levy. Central Curry's budget didn't break this out as its own category; consider whether to normalize these into 'state' or 'local' for cross-district comparison, or keep as a fourth bucket.

other.note: unappropriated_ending_fund_balance ($1.8M, ~8% of expenditures) is the deliberately-tapering reserve described in the budget message highlights -- worth keeping visible as its own line rather than folding silently into 'other,' since the district itself is treating it as a a strategic, shrinking cushion, not routine spending.

app_display_guidance.suggested_grouping: Same Instruction / Support Services / Other framing as Central Curry, for a consistent cross-district comparison.
app_display_guidance.good_pull_quote_for_app: BHSD's own budget message states plainly that Oregon districts are funded based on enrollment, that BHSD's enrollment is in slow long-term decline, and that this year's budget cuts nearly 16 combined licensed and classified positions as a direct result -- while leaning on two one-time revenue sources (delayed forest fee payments and fund carryover) that won't be there next year, with $1.7 million in further cuts already anticipated for 2026-27.
app_display_guidance.biggest_single_program: Office of the Principal (school-level administration across the district's schools) is the single largest support-services line at $1,631,098 -- consistent with the same pattern seen in Central Curry's budget, where principal's office spending outweighs technology, fiscal services, or superintendent's office individually.
app_display_guidance.scale_note: Brookings-Harbor's General Fund ($21.68M) is roughly 2.8x the size of Central Curry's ($7.68M), consistent with its much larger enrollment (~1,300+ students vs. ~240) -- useful context if the app shows districts side by side, so the size difference doesn't read as one district being better- or worse-funded per student without that context.
